content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to PMP Certification in San Jose

steps_items.heading: Confirm Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: PMI requires either a four-year degree with three years of project-management experience, or a high-school diploma with five years of experience. Review PMI's formal education and professional-experience criteria to confirm you meet the baseline for application. Document your project hours and leadership roles.

steps_items.heading: Complete 35 Contact Hours of Training
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual, instructor-led PMP Certification Training course. Our curriculum covers the PMBOK® Guide, exam domains, and real-world application. Attend all sessions synchronously, engage with active certified practitioners, and receive course materials and recordings for review.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: After completing your 35 contact hours, submit your formal PMP application directly to PMI. Provide your education credentials, project-experience summary, and proof of course completion from Granite PM Academy. Pay the associated PMI exam fee and await eligibility verification before scheduling your exam.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Sit for the Exam
steps_items.text: Granite PM Academy provides targeted exam-preparation resources, practice questions, and strategies to reinforce your knowledge. Schedule your proctored exam through Pearson VUE once PMI approves your application. Apply test-taking techniques, manage your time across 180 questions, and demonstrate mastery of project-management domains.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your PMP Credential
steps_items.text: The PMP credential renews on a three-year cycle. Earn Professional Development Units (PDUs) through approved training, conference attendance, volunteer work, or published articles. Stay current with PMI membership and submit your renewal documentation before your expiration date to keep your credential active.

fq_items.question: Do I need to travel to {city} for this training?
fq_items.answer: No. All of our PMP training is delivered live-virtual via video conference, so {city} professionals attend from wherever they work. No commuting or hotel required.

fq_items.question: What are the PMP eligibility requirements?
fq_items.answer: PMI sets four eligibility paths based on education: a secondary diploma (high school or equivalent) requires 60 months of project leadership experience; an associate's degree requires 48 months; a bachelor's degree requires 36 months; and a bachelor's or postgraduate degree from a PMI Global Accreditation Center (GAC)-accredited program requires just 24 months. Every path also requires 35 hours of project management education — our course satisfies this requirement in full.

fq_items.question: How long does it take to get PMP certified in {city}?
fq_items.answer: After completing training, PMI typically approves applications within 5–10 business days. Once approved, you have one year to sit for the exam. Most students study 4–8 weeks after the course before scheduling their exam.

fq_items.question: What is your pass guarantee?
fq_items.answer: If you complete our course and do not pass the PMP exam within 90 days, we provide additional coaching sessions at no additional cost until you pass.

fq_items.question: Is this training PMI-approved?
fq_items.answer: Yes. Granite PM Academy is a PMI Premier Authorized Training Partner (ATP). Our curriculum is aligned to PMI’s current Examination Content Outline and our contact hours are fully accepted by PMI.

fq_items.question: Is PMP certification worth it for project managers in San Jose's tech sector?
fq_items.answer: San Jose's concentration of major tech employers—Cisco, Adobe, PayPal, Zoom, and others—often run large, cross-functional infrastructure and product programs where PMP® certification demonstrates structured program governance. While Agile and Scrum credentials compete for attention in software-heavy roles, the PMP® credential signals mastery of traditional and hybrid methodologies valued in hardware, cloud infrastructure, and enterprise-scale initiatives. National data shows PMP®-certified professionals report a median salary premium versus non-certified peers, a gap that typically holds across regions including high-cost markets like San Jose.

fq_items.question: Which San Jose industries and employers value PMP certification most?
fq_items.answer: San Jose's dominant sectors—semiconductor and electronic design automation (EDA), networking infrastructure, fintech, and video communications—frequently require PMP® certification for mid- to senior-level program and operations roles. Employers managing complex product roadmaps, distributed teams, and multi-year initiatives especially value the credential. However, software-first organizations may prioritize Agile certifications alongside or instead of PMP®. Understanding your target role's job posting patterns in your industry helps clarify whether PMP® is your primary credential or a complementary one.

fq_items.question: Can I attend PMP training in San Jose while working full-time in tech?
fq_items.answer: Granite PM Academy's live-virtual format lets you attend from your home, office, or any location with internet access—removing commute friction common in San Jose's congested corridors. This flexibility suits full-time professionals at tech companies who need to balance certification study with demanding project schedules. Live-virtual sessions also mean you can join from your workspace during lunch, before hours, or from remote locations without disrupting your current role.

fq_items.question: When should San Jose project managers pursue PMP certification in a competitive job market?
fq_items.answer: San Jose's dense cluster of major tech employers creates year-round hiring for program management roles, but certification timing matters. Pursuing PMP® certification while employed allows you to apply learning immediately to your current programs and build verifiable experience. If you're planning a role transition within the region's tech, infrastructure, or fintech sectors, completing the credential before a job search positions you competitively. Starting early—ideally 6–12 months before your target move—gives you time to gain hands-on project hours while studying.
